milestones.name: Set up the worktree

actions.label: EXPLAIN
actions.title: Keep the desk and app separate
actions.body: Branch 00 contains this presenter desk, instructions and reference code. The runnable apps live on branches 02 and 03. Keep the desk open while working in a second checkout.

actions.label: DO
actions.title: Start the presenter desk
actions.body: From the branch 00 checkout, run the command below and open http://localhost:4410. No API key or dependency installation is needed for the desk. Keep this terminal running.

actions.label: DO
actions.title: Create the application worktree
actions.body: In another terminal in the presenter repository, fetch the remote branches and create your local working branch from chapter 2. This works after a fresh clone. If the rehearsal folder already exists, inspect git worktree list and reuse it.
actions.command:
git fetch origin
git worktree add --no-track -b ai-devcraft/live-demo ../incident-management-live origin/ai-devcraft/02-backend-agents
cd ../incident-management-live
code .
git worktree list

actions.label: DO
actions.title: Prepare the application
actions.body: In the new application checkout, install dependencies. Create .env only if absent and set OPENROUTER_API_KEY privately. Keep credentials off screen.
actions.command:
pnpm install
# Only if .env is absent:
cp .env.example .env

actions.label: DO
actions.title: Start chapter 2
actions.body: Stop any other demo app using the same ports, then run pnpm dev in the application checkout. Open Angular on 4300 and Mastra Studio on 4211. The presenter desk remains on 4410. Rehearse both prompts here: each worktree has separate databases and Studio history.

milestones.recovery: Keep the presenter desk on branch 00 and run the app from the second worktree. Use git worktree list to locate an existing rehearsal folder; do not delete it or discard its changes. Stop only the conflicting server before restarting on the same port.

milestones.name: Follow the request

actions.label: SHOW
actions.title: Start in the Angular app
actions.body: Show the readings table and Your question field. Point out date/time, shift manager, room, metric, value and condition. Say: “The user asks for a different selection of readings without us adding another filter control.”

actions.label: OPEN
actions.title: Trace the HTTP request
actions.body: Open `apps/angular-host/src/app/domains/facility/data/facility-client.ts` and find investigate. This ordinary Angular form sends the question to POST /api/investigate. There is no CopilotKit or AG-UI on this branch.

actions.label: OPEN
actions.title: Follow it into Mastra
actions.body: Open `apps/facility-service/src/investigate-historian.ts`. The facility creates a run of historianQueryWorkflow and passes the question as input. This UI starts a known workflow directly; it is not asking a chat agent to choose a tool.

milestones.recovery: Inspect the actual SQL and the failed check. If the provider is unavailable, show a rehearsed Studio run and identify it as such. Stop the running demo before restarting it. Do not reset databases or discard changes during the talk.

Show the four .then calls together: generate, deterministic check, agentic check, validate and execute. The step functions follow below. There is no automatic repair loop in this version.

actions.label: OPEN
actions.title: Read the generator prompt
actions.body: Open `apps/agent-service/src/mastra/workflows/historian-query/agents/sql-generator-agent.ts`. Show the schema, catalog and structured output: SQL plus an explanation. The generator sees schema information, not actual database rows.

actions.label: EXPLAIN
actions.title: Keep the complete reading
actions.body: For highest and lowest queries, return the complete stored row with all eleven columns. This preserves the room, timestamp and metric. MAX, MIN and AVG are allowed, but an aggregate across several readings may have no single room or timestamp.

This is an early check; database enforcement still follows.

milestones.name: Review with Jev

actions.label: OPEN
actions.title: Three checks, one request
actions.body: Open `apps/agent-service/src/mastra/workflows/historian-query/agents/jev-sql-reviewer.ts` at createJevSqlReviewFunction. Start with the composition of createSafetyCheck, createIntentCheck and createColumnCheck. The question and SQL go to typesafe/jev-1.13 through one OpenRouter decisions request.

actions.label: OPEN
actions.title: Read the three questions
actions.body: In `apps/agent-service/src/mastra/workflows/historian-query/agents/jev-sql-reviewer.ts`, scroll to the three functions at the bottom. Is the SQL read-only and within the allowed data? Does it answer the human’s question? Does it return all and only the expected columns? Aggregations are allowed when returned through existing columns.

actions.label: EXPLAIN
actions.title: Show the decision rule
actions.body: Each Noul value is between 0 and 1. Our demo approves only when all three are greater than 0.5. The concerns list names checks that did not pass. Jev does not provide a written explanation; those messages come from our application. The generator explanation is separate.

actions.label: OPEN

milestones.name: Demo: rejection

actions.label: DO
actions.title: Ask for missing data
actions.body: In Angular, enter the prompt below and click Find readings. Expand Query and review. We have shift-manager names, but no email-address column.
actions.command: Show the email address of each shift manager.

actions.label: SHOW
actions.title: Inspect the same Studio run
actions.body: Open historianQueryWorkflow in Studio and select the run whose input matches the question. Show generate-sql and preflight-sql. The verified proposal returned names with NULL metadata; that read-only SELECT passed preflight.

actions.label: SHOW
actions.title: Show where Jev rejects it
actions.body: Open review-sql output: review.approved is false, and concerns contains “Jev did not approve the intent check.” A safe query still needs to answer the question.

actions.label: EXPLAIN
actions.title: A rejection is a handled result
actions.body: Show final status rejected and stage reviewer. The final step returns before database execution. Studio may mark the overall run successful because rejection is a normal workflow result. A table from a previous request is not new output. If a new run differs, explain its actual failed check rather than claiming the same result.

prompts.title: Rejected: missing email data
prompts.prompt: Show the email address of each shift manager.
prompts.before: Enter this in Your question in Angular and click Find readings.
prompts.expected: The verified run passed preflight, then Jev rejected the intent check. No database execution.
prompts.inspect: Show generated SQL, review.approved: false and the failed intent check. Final result: status rejected, stage reviewer. Overall workflow success can still mean a handled rejection.

milestones.recovery: Inspect the actual SQL and the failed check. If the provider is unavailable, show a rehearsed Studio run and identify it as such. Stop the running demo before restarting it. Do not reset databases or discard changes during the talk.

milestones.name: Demo: successful query

actions.label: DO
actions.title: Ask for each manager’s highest reading
actions.body: Return to Your question in Angular, enter the prompt below and click Find readings.
actions.command: Show the highest air temperature for each shift manager.

actions.label: SHOW
actions.title: Show all table columns
actions.body: The verified seeded-data run returned three rows, one per manager. Point out that date/time, room, metric, value and condition are filled automatically.

actions.label: SHOW
actions.title: Read the generated SQL
actions.body: Expand Query and review. Show the Air temperature filter and how the query selects a complete highest reading per manager. The verified SQL used ROW_NUMBER, with latest timestamp and reading ID as tie-breakers. Read the actual generated query; SQL can vary.

actions.label: SHOW
actions.title: Trace the approved run
actions.body: In Studio, match the input and show generate-sql → preflight-sql → review-sql → deterministic-validate-and-execute. Show approved: true, an empty concerns list and final status executed with the readings. These outputs do not expose raw Noul values.

actions.label: TRANSITION
actions.title: Return to the Angular result
actions.body: Finish on the populated table. Say: “Now we have the backend workflow. Next, we add CopilotKit and AG-UI so the frontend can participate in the interaction.”

prompts.title: Approved: highest temperature
prompts.prompt: Show the highest air temperature for each shift manager.
prompts.before: Use the same Angular form after the rejected request.
prompts.expected: The verified seeded-data run returned three complete readings, one per manager. Date/time, room, metric, value and condition are populated.
prompts.inspect: Show the SQL, all four workflow steps, review.approved: true, empty concerns and final status executed. Return to the populated Angular table.

milestones.name: Chapter 3: switch to CopilotKit

actions.label: DO
actions.title: Switch the application worktree
actions.body: Stop pnpm dev with Ctrl+C in the application terminal. Keep the presenter desk running in its separate checkout. Save any changes first. Create this local branch once; on later rehearsals use git switch ai-devcraft/live-ui.
actions.command:
git fetch origin
git switch --no-track -c ai-devcraft/live-ui origin/ai-devcraft/03-agentic-ui
pnpm install
pnpm dev

actions.label: SHOW

actions.body: Say: “The same backend is now a tool in a conversation. The frontend can show progress, change the view and pause an alarm proposal for a human decision.” There is no A2UI example in this chapter.

milestones.name: Demo: human approval

actions.label: DO
actions.title: Check the alarm before the demo
actions.body: Select Snapshot and inspect Packaging hall → Air temperature. It should say not raised. If a previous rehearsal already raised it, resolve that demo alarm with the normal UI before presenting, or use another unraised metric and adapt the prompt. Keep the audit.

actions.label: DO
actions.title: Ask for an alarm proposal
actions.body: Enter the prompt below. Pause when the approval card appears. Show room, metric, reason and operator. The alarm has not been raised yet.
actions.command: Raise an alarm for the Packaging hall air temperature because I want the operator to investigate.

actions.label: SHOW
actions.title: Reject first
actions.body: Click Reject. Show Rejected · no alarm was raised, the rejected audit entry and the resumed assistant acknowledgment. The active alarm count must not increase.

actions.label: DO
actions.title: Create a new proposal
actions.body: Ask again using the prompt below. A new proposal needs a new human decision.
actions.command: Please propose that alarm again for Packaging hall air temperature. I want to approve it this time.

actions.label: SHOW
actions.title: Approve and inspect the outcome
actions.body: Click Approve and raise alarm. Show Approved · alarm raised, the active alarm count increasing by one, the approved audit entry and the assistant acknowledgment. Approval and execution are distinct: an already-active alarm produces an execution-failed outcome.

actions.label: EXPLAIN
actions.title: Name the demo boundary
actions.body: The facility backend performs the write and records both decisions. This workshop uses the fixed demo operator night-reception; it does not implement production authentication or role-based authorization.

prompts.title: Request human approval
prompts.prompt: Raise an alarm for the Packaging hall air temperature because I want the operator to investigate.
prompts.before: Enter this in the Factory assistant chat on branch 03.
prompts.expected: A card waits for Reject or Approve and raise alarm. Nothing is raised merely by proposing it.
prompts.inspect: Show the corresponding UI result and the actual tool output in Mastra Studio.

milestones.name: Walk through human approval

actions.label: OPEN
actions.title: Register the human step
actions.body: At the end of connect-facility-agent.ts, show review_alarm, its schema and AlarmApprovalCard. This is the pause point exposed to the agent.

actions.label: OPEN
actions.title: Follow the human click
actions.body: In AlarmApprovalCard, follow decide: validate the proposal against the facility catalog, wait for the operator, call the store, then pass the recorded outcome to toolCall.respond. Both approval and rejection resume the conversation.

actions.label: OPEN
actions.title: Follow the backend write
actions.body: Open facility-store.ts → decideAlarmApproval and facility-client.ts → decideAlarmApproval in the app checkout. Follow POST /api/alarm-approvals in server.ts into repository.ts. The transaction checks the metric, records the decision and creates an alarm only when approved.

actions.label: SHOW
actions.title: Explain retries with one concrete example
actions.body: The message/tool-call identity remains stable when the card reopens or a request is retried. The backend returns the recorded result for that same decision rather than creating a second alarm. A conflicting decision is rejected.

actions.label: SHOW
actions.title: Close with the failure paths
actions.body: An invalid proposal can be dismissed without executing it, so the conversation can continue. A failed HTTP request shows an error and allows retry. An approved but failed alarm operation is displayed as failed, not as success.
